cues.text: This is Walt. Walt plays forty-two.
He can see his own seven dominoes... and nothing else.
The other twenty-one could be dealt three hundred ninety-nine million ways.
And every one of those deals can play out billions of different ways.
Write them all down, and you'd fill ten million hard drives. For one move!
So Walt doesn't try everything. He tries a handful.
He imagines one possible deal. Nobody at that table thinks hard. They just check a little handbook.
Been here before? Do what the book says. Never seen it? Roll a die, and scribble it down.
No peeking. Each player only knows their own hand.
Forty imagined deals later, Walt counts. How often did we make the bid?
Then he levels up. Dice aren't very smart. So now, instead of rolling, everyone picks their best play.
Forty little worlds. One pretty good move. Small enough to fit in your pocket.
And that's how Walt sees forty-two.
